summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and gastrostomy status was admitted after transfer for a clogged GJ tube. He had recently been treated for aspiration pneumonia with Unasyn and was weaned from mechanical ventilation and pressors prior to admission. The clogged feeding tube was successfully replaced via interventional radiology, allowing resumption of tube feeds and oral medications, including antiretroviral therapy. Mild transaminitis was noted with ultrasound showing gallstones but no cholecystitis; outpatient follow-up was recommended. He remained stable on trach collar with no respiratory deterioration. He was discharged to extended care with plans for ongoing monitoring of liver enzymes and continuation of chronic medications.
problems: Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase and lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
